Keywords: House of Capet Fleur de Lis
RagShortTexts: The Capetian dynasty expanded the royal demesne under Louis IX's revered Christian justice.

Variants.Content: Ruling France since 987 without an interrupted succession, the House of Capet reached unprecedented moral authority under Louis IX. Emblazoned with golden fleurs-de-lis on azure fields, royal bodies lay enshrined at Saint-Denis. Louis centralized justice through itinerant royal inspectors (enquêteurs) and the Parlement of Paris.
Cadet branches like Anjou and Artois extended Capetian dynastic dominance into southern Italy and crusader principalities, establishing Paris as the diplomatic arbitrator of Christendom.
Commoners revere King Louis dispensing open-air justice beneath the Oak of Vincennes, where any aggrieved pauper can petition the crown without aristocratic intimidation.
